Iḍaguñji
------------------------------------------
Gaṇapati or गणेश is one of the most popular deities of Hindu religion. According to the Hindu scriptures he along with his मोथेर् Durgā—is the god to be worshipped in this age for quick results!
In India, there are eight गणपति temples in eight places known as siddhiprada-kṣetras (places of पिल्ग्रिमगे giving quick results for prayers). The गणपति temple at इडगुञ्जि in Northern Karnataka is one such.
The small town of इडगुञ्जि is situated at a distance of 12 kms. (8 miles) from the bigger coastal town of Honnavara on the banks of Śarāvatī river of the world famous Jog-falls.
The temple town was originally known as Iḍā-kuñju, meaning “a forest on the left side (of the river).” This name gradually became इडगुञ्जि.
As per the sthaḷapurāṇa or local legend, the वालखिल्यस्, the diminutive sages, were doing तपस् (austerities) here. But they were frequently troubled by herds of elephants. So they requested the sage नारद to help them, by bringing गणपति from कैलास. Since the boy गणपति was fond of pañcakajjāya (a kind of sweet prepared out of five ingredients), नारद managed to bring him to the forest of इडगुञ्जि by tempting him with that sweet. As he finally agreed to stay there permanently, a beautiful image was prepared by the divine sculptor विश्वकर्म into which he entered through his spiritual power. And, a temple was built round it. All the gods also started living here in their subtle bodies.
Round the temple, विष्णु, शिव and ब्रह्मा created three tīrthas or holy water wells, known as चक्रतीर्थ, Śūlatīrtha and Kamaṇḍalutīrtha which exist even today.
The image is a rare one in the standing posture, with only two hands, holding a lotus and a modaka (a sweetmeat). There is only one more similar image at गोकर्ण.
The temple is a beautiful structure with the kaḷaśa (pineal) on the gopuram being gold-plated.
The main festivals are गणेश- caturthī (Bhādrapada-śukla-caturthī, generally in September) and Saṅkaṣṭa- caturthī (caturthī of kṛṣṇapakṣa or dark fortnight of every month). If the latter happens to come on Tuesday, it is called Aṅgārakacaturthī and is observed in a special way. The रथोत्सव or temple- car-festival is held during रथसप्तमी (generally in February).
Attached to the temple there is a Saṁskṛtapāṭhaśālā (Sanskrit School) running a course spread over five years. The students are provided free board and lodging.
Iḍaguñji is famous for the art of यक्षगान (a type of folk-drama), this गणपति being the presiding deity for that art.

iḍā
------------------------------------------
Nāḍīs are passages in the body that carry the prāṇic energy. According to the works on हठयोग, there are 3,50,000 of them in the human body. Of these, fourteen are considered as the principal ones, out of which again, three are most important. They are iḍā, पिङ्गला and सुषुम्ना.
The iḍā starts from the left nostril and runs up to the मूलाधार-चक्र, at the base of the spine. It is also called ‘candra or मोओन्’.
It has an important role to play in प्राणायाम.
See also PIṄGALĀ, PRĀṆĀYĀMA and SUṢUMNĀ.
The Ṛgvedic goddess Iḷā is also spelt as ‘Iḍā’. See IḶĀ for details.
In वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, iḍā is the portion cut up from an oblatory material, sprinkled with आज्य (ghee) and consumed by all the participants together.
